newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai PM exudes confidence on eve of debate.
newsitem.headline: Thai PM exudes confidence on eve of debate.

text.p: Thai prime minister Banharn Silpa-archa brimmed with confidence on the eve of a no-confidence debate against him as the opposition on Tuesday threatened him with ruin if he went through the process.
"I am 100 percent confident," he told reporters after chairing a brief weekly cabinet meeting at government house. "I am going home now for the final preparations."
The premier also went to see Thailand's top Buddhist monk in Bangkok to receive blessings ahead of the debate.
Banharn's 14-month-old, six-party coalition government has been under sharp attack by the opposition and the local media over its handling of the economy and domestic politics.
The televised debate on the no-confidence motion tabled by the opposition starts on Wednesday and could last for more than two days, political analysts said.
The motion accuses Banharn of incompetence and economic mismanagement, among other things. He has denied the charges.

Speculation was rife in the run-up to the debate that Banharn might quit, hand over the premiership to a more acceptable politician or even dissolve parliament before the debate, but he has until now done nothing along those lines.
Some analysts expect Banharn to win the debate with the support of his coalition, which controls 209 of the 391 seats in parliament.

But secretary general of the main opposition Democrat Party, Sanan Kachonprasart, told reporters Banharn's political foes planned to attack him on doubts over his nationality and eligibility to remain as the country's prime minister.

The opposition said it also planned to hurt Banharn with allegations he was born in China and emigrated to Thailand with his family in 1937. As the constitution states only those born in Thailand could run in general elections, he might not be eligible to remain premier, it added.
"After the debate the opposition plans to file complaints against him to the authorities," said Sanan.
Banharn denied this and vowed to fight the accusation.
But Sanoh Thienthong, secretary general of Banharn's core Chart Thai party, warned the opposition against hitting the premier below the belt.
Earlier, in a newspaper interview published on Tuessday Banharn said that he would not resign and was ready to face the no-confidence motion tabled against him in parliament.

"I have said all along that I am not tied to the position (of prime minister). But this does not mean I will back down," Banharn told the Bangkok Post. "I am prepared to answer all questions from the accusations that I interfered, mismanagement of personnel, to poor economic performance."
Barharn also told the Post that if he won the vote he would revamp his economic team to address urgent economic concerns. Thailand has seen an economic slowdown this year.
"Let me say this. If I pass through this (debate), there will be definite change in the economic sphere, especially a new economic team," he said.

Banharn said recent declines in the Thai stock market were precipitated by his foes, whom he accused of dumping shares to force the market down and discredit him ahead of the debate. The Thai bourse has been near three-year-lows since early September.
